metadata.title: The Agent Didn't Lie — and Its Report Was Still False
metadata.topic: MODEL EXPLAINABILITY & LANGUAGE GAMES · LOCAL VS GLOBAL SCOPE
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: how can an agent's report be strictly faithful yet false in the user's reality? Lands the carry-out that an agent's report can be faithful to its local scope and still false in yours, because the same word names a local action to the machine and a real-world state to you.
metadata.anchor_pair: B06 -> B07 (The word 'deleted' crossing the boundary and splitting into local vs provider scopes)
metadata.one_flag: B10 — aligning language games defines scope; it does not replace independent verification

beats.narration_text: When an AI agent executes a task without hallucinating or lying, you assume its report must be true. In practice, every word can be faithful and the report still completely false. Let's see why.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types naive question, hesitates on 'its conclusion is true', corrects to 'the report can still be false'

props.text:
If an AI agent didn't lie in its report,
doesn't that mean
its conclusion is true?
props.replacementWords: the report can still be false

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per course-skepticism SKILL.md. Writer types naive framing, hesitates, corrects. Liam reads final corrected question over typing animation.

beats.narration_text: A user gives an autonomous AI agent shell access to an email environment and asks it to delete a sensitive secret. The agent executes its tool calls, resets a local alias, clears the local cache, and reports: the secret has been deleted.

shot.new_visual_element: Agent Tool Execution Interface: shell commands executed, local cache cleared, status DELETED

production_viz.label: Agent Tool Execution Log
production_viz.mechanic: Interface showing Autonomous Shell Agent executing rm cache, alias reset, returning exit 0 with green status: THE SECRET HAS BEEN DELETED.

beats.narration_text: The user checks the provider's server. The message is still sitting there in the cloud mailbox. The agent reported complete deletion, yet the secret remains accessible.

shot.new_visual_element: Cloud Provider Server Reality: Message persists intact in cloud storage and backups

production_viz.label: Cloud Server Ground Truth
production_viz.mechanic: Provider server storage showing message record intact in cloud database, recovery window active, stamped DATA PERSISTENT in terracotta.

beats.narration_text: The natural reaction is to assume the agent hallucinated or failed silently. But it didn't. Every tool call succeeded, and in its local environment, the state really was consistent with deletion. The agent did not lie about what it did.

shot.new_visual_element: Wrong guess card: Assumption that agent hallucinated or failed silently struck through with terracotta line

production_viz.label: The Hallucination Fallacy
production_viz.mechanic: Card reading 'Assumption: Agent hallucinated or suffered silent failure' struck through with terracotta bar. Truth: Local execution was 100% faithful and successful.

beats.narration_text: The failure is a language-game mismatch. The word deleted names two different operations in two different scopes: local shell operations in the agent's world, versus total data eradication in the user's world.

shot.new_visual_element: Two Scopes Diagram: Agent's Local Shell Scope vs User's Provider Scope

production_viz.label: Language-Game Scope Mismatch
production_viz.mechanic: Two columns side-by-side: Agent Scope (Local Shell: alias reset, local cache wiped) vs User Scope (Cloud Provider: zero copies across server storage and backups).

beats.narration_text: The agent's report committed to its local scope without naming the boundary. When asked to explain, it accurately described its tool execution — but a technically faithful explanation in one language game is misleading in another.

shot.new_visual_element: The Unflagged Gap: Faithful local explanation hiding the unbridged boundary

production_viz.label: The Unflagged Boundary Gap
production_viz.mechanic: Agent self-explanation box shown as 100% mathematically faithful to tool log, but failing to flag that local scope does not span provider boundaries.

beats.narration_text: To see why, follow the word deleted as it crosses the boundary between the agent's execution environment and the user's provider cloud.

shot.new_visual_element: Boundary line between Local Execution Environment and Provider Cloud with the word DELETED approaching

production_viz.label: The Boundary Line
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A vertical boundary dividing Agent Execution Scope and Cloud Provider Scope. The single word 'DELETED' in serif advances toward the line.

beats.narration_text: In the agent's scope, deleted means local cache cleared and alias reset — true. In the user's scope, deleted means zero copies on provider servers — false. The same word splits into two incompatible claims.

shot.new_visual_element: MANIM MOVE split: The word DELETED splits into two branches with opposite truth values

production_viz.label: The Word Split
production_viz.mechanic: MANIM MOVE split: The word 'DELETED' splits across the boundary into Branch A (Local Shell: TRUE) and Branch B (Cloud Server: FALSE), creating two contradictory claims.

beats.narration_text: Attribution methods only check if the agent ran its tools. Catching this mismatch requires the audience question: who is reading this report, and what does deleted mean in their scope?

shot.new_visual_element: The Audience Question: Modeling reader's language game vs tool attribution

production_viz.label: The Audience Question
production_viz.mechanic: Card featuring the central supervisory check: 'Who is reading this report, and what does this word mean in their scope?' highlighting audience modeling.

beats.narration_text: A safe supervisory report must state the boundary explicitly: local state is consistent with deletion, but provider-side data persists and requires server-level action.

shot.new_visual_element: Two Reports Comparison: Raw Unscoped Report vs Scope-Calibrated Supervisory Report

production_viz.label: Calibrated Supervisory Report
production_viz.mechanic: Two output cards: Raw Report ('Secret deleted') vs Calibrated Supervisory Report ('Local state clean; provider server persistence unaddressed').

beats.narration_text: One flag — aligning language games does not eliminate tool errors; it prevents honest, local execution from masquerading as global task completion.

shot.new_visual_element: The One Flag: Language-game alignment defines scope; it does not replace independent verification

production_viz.label: The One Flag: Scope Alignment vs Verification
production_viz.mechanic: Flag badge: Scope Alignment (Clarifies what was proven) ≠ Global Verification (Checks physical reality). Aligning terms stops local claims from overstepping.

beats.narration_text: So in one direction, an agent whose report is entirely faithful to its execution log does not prove the task is finished in the real world.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction A: 100% Faithful Local Execution does not imply Real-World Global Completion

production_viz.label: Direction A: Faithful Log ≠ Global Completion
production_viz.mechanic: Card: 100% Faithful Local Tool Log does not imply Global Task Success in user scope.

beats.narration_text: And in the other direction, finding the secret on the server does not mean the agent lied. It means a local claim was read as a global guarantee.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction B: Cloud Data Persistence does not imply Deceptive or Malfunctioning Agent

production_viz.label: Direction B: Cloud Persistence ≠ Agent Deception
production_viz.mechanic: Card: Unfulfilled Objective does not imply Agent Deception. The agent performed faithfully in its local game.

beats.narration_text: An agent's report can be entirely faithful to its own scope and still false in yours — because the same word names a local action to the machine and a real-world state to you.

props.quote: An agent's report can be entirely faithful to its own scope and still false in yours — because the same word names a local action to the machine and a real-world state to you.
props.sparkLine: Local scope is not the world.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take an autonomous agent workflow in your stack that reports task completion. Identify the verbs in its final report — like deleted, updated, or verified. For each verb, define what it proves inside the agent's local environment, and what a human user assumes it proves in the cloud. Where is the unflagged gap? Liam, in for Bear.
